yieldInfo1: The quantity of the recipes you combined is used to calculate how much the cake cost (the sum of everything that went into it).

yieldInfoExample: The cake cost R$ 40 and yields 10 slices → each slice costs R$ 4. From that, the app suggests the selling price.
yieldInfo3: Without the yield, the app knows the cost of the whole cake but can't tell how much to charge per slice. That's why the two fields complement each other — they're not the same information.

pricingTutorial:
How to register ingredients correctly

When registering an ingredient, always enter the real purchase, not the amount used in the recipe.

Main rule:
Purchased quantity = the whole package/purchase
Total amount paid = price of the whole package/purchase
Unit = the same unit you want to use for the calculation

Examples:

Flour, 1 kg bought for R$ 5.89:
Purchased quantity: 1000
Unit: g
Total amount paid: 5.89

Milk, 1 liter bought for R$ 5.99:
Purchased quantity: 1000
Unit: ml
Total amount paid: 5.99

Oil, 1 liter bought for R$ 6.57:
Purchased quantity: 1000
Unit: ml
Total amount paid: 6.57

Baking powder, 100 g bought for R$ 5.20:
Purchased quantity: 100
Unit: g
Total amount paid: 5.20

Condensed milk, 1 can of 395 g for R$ 7.50:
Package type: Can
Weight per package: 395
Base unit: g
Purchased quantity: 1
Total amount paid: 7.50

In the recipe, if you use 4 cans:
Quantity used: 4
Unit: un

What not to do:
Don't register 1 g with the price of the whole package, unless you really bought 1 gram.

Don't register a box/tray as un if, in the recipe, un means an individual item.

For strawberries, prefer weight:
Package type: Tray
Weight per package: 380
Base unit: g
Purchased quantity: 1
Total amount paid: price of the tray

In the recipe:
Quantity used: approximate weight of the strawberries
Unit: g

Summary:
Use g for dry ingredients, ml for liquids and un only when the purchased and used unit are the same thing.
